rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī identifies Sūrat al-Masad as Meccan.
rows.anchor: سورة المسد مكية بسم الله الرحمان الرحيم

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Abū Lahab asked what he would receive for believing; when told he would receive what Muslims receive, he rejected a religion that made him their equal, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: حكاه عبد الرحمن بن زيد أن أبا لهب أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After the warning to his near relatives, the Prophet called people to al-Ṣafā and warned of imminent punishment; Abū Lahab cursed him, and the sūra was revealed.
rows.anchor: ما رواه ابن عباس أنه لما نزل { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين } أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصفا

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن كيسان
rows.claim: Abū Lahab turned visiting delegations away by calling the Prophet a lying sorcerer or mad; after one delegation persisted, he again maligned the Prophet, who grieved and received this sūra.
rows.anchor: ما حكاه عبد الرحمن بن كيسان أنه كان إذا وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفد انطلق إليهم أبو لهب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses تَبَّتْ as having failed or come to naught.
rows.anchor: أحدها : خابت ،   قاله ابن عباس .

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ explains تَبَّتْ as having gone astray.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ضلّت ،   وهو قول عطاء .

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr explains تَبَّتْ as having perished.
rows.anchor: الثالث : هلكت ،   قاله ابن جبير .

rows.speaker: يمان بن رئاب
rows.claim: Yamān ibn Riʾāb says تَبَّتْ means becoming empty of every good thing.
rows.anchor: الرابع : صفِرت من كل خير ،   قاله يمان بن رئاب .

rows.speaker: الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī transmits from Abū ʿAmr a chant reportedly heard after ʿUthmān’s killing, ending with an imprecation using تَبًّا.
rows.anchor: حكى الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء أنه لما قتل عثمان بن عفان سمع الناس هاتفاً يقول :

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses تَبَّتْ as having lost; the cited anonymous verse uses تَبًّا in a curse.
rows.anchor: الخامس : خسرت ،   قاله قتادة ،   ومنه قول الشاعر : تواعَدَني قوْمي ليَسْعوْا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes Abū Lahab’s two hands to mean Abū Lahab himself, since a person may be expressed by the hand; the cited phrase in 22:10 likewise means the person.
rows.anchor: يعني نفس أبي لهب ،   وقد يعبر عن النفس باليد ،   كما قال تعالى { ذلك بما قدمت يداك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the hands as Abū Lahab’s deeds, which are attributed to the hands because actions are usually performed with them.
rows.anchor: أي عمل أبي لهب ،   وإنما نسب العمل إلى اليد ؛ لأنه في الأكثر يكون بها .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that Abū Lahab was given this kunya for his beauty and his glowing, flame-like cheeks.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه كني أبا لهب لحسنه وتلهب وجنته ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for using Abū Lahab’s kunya is that he was better known by it than by his personal name.
rows.anchor: أنه كان بكنيته أشهر منه باسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that his given name identified him as a servant of an idol, reportedly ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, so the sūra avoids it.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان مسمى بعبد صنم ،   وقيل : إنه عبد العزى ،   فلذلك عدل عنه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation says a personal name is nobler than a kunya, which refers to someone through another person; God therefore names His prophets by their names.
rows.anchor: لأن الاسم أشرف من الكنية ؛ لأن الكنية إشارة إليه باسم غيره ،   ولذلك دعا الله أنبياءه بأسمائهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes وَتَبَّ as emphasis repeating the preceding curse on Abū Lahab’s hands.
rows.anchor: أنه تأكيد للأول من قوله :{ تبت يدا أبي لهب } ، فقال بعده :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says his hands were ruined when God prevented him from harming the Messenger, while he himself perished through the painful punishment awaiting him with God.
rows.anchor: يعني تبت يدا أبي لهب بما منعه الله تعالى من أذى لرسوله ،   وتب بما له عند الله من أليم عقابه .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes وَتَبَّ to mean that Abū Lahab had already perished.
rows.anchor: يعني قد تبّ ،   قاله ابن عباس .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets وَتَبَّ to mean that Abū Lahab’s offspring also perished.
rows.anchor: يعني وتبّ ولد أبي لهب ،   قاله مجاهد .

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads وقد تب instead of وَتَبَّ, making the ending a statement; the other reading is a curse like the opening.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : ( تبت يدا أبي لهبٍ وقد تب ) ، جعله خبراً ،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Abū Lahab’s hands perished away from monotheism.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : عن التوحيد ،   قاله ابن عباس .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says Abū Lahab’s hands perished away from good deeds.
rows.anchor: الثاني : عن الخيرات ،   قاله مجاهد .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ is that his wealth did not ward anything off from him.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : ما دفع عنه .

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ as meaning that his wealth did not benefit him.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ما نفعه ،   قاله الضحاك .

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says his مال was his herds, since Abū Lahab owned grazing livestock.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أراد أغنامه ؛ لأنه كان صاحب سائمة ،   قاله أبو العالية .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view understands his wealth as both inherited property (talīd) and acquired property (ṭārif).
rows.anchor: أنه أراد تليده وطارفه ،   والتليد : الموروث ،   والطارف : المكتسب .

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets what Abū Lahab earned as his wicked deeds.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : عمله الخبيث ،   قاله الضحاك .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets what he earned as his children.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ولده ،   قاله ابن عباس .

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says, “Your children are among your earnings,” supporting the interpretation of what he earned as offspring.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال :  "  أولادكم من كسبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Lahab’s son ʿUtba matched his father’s hostility: after Sūrat al-Najm was revealed, he blasphemed, spat at the Prophet, and left for Syria; the Prophet prayed against him, and a lion killed him.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  اللهم سلط عليه كلباً من كلابك  "  ،   فأكله الأسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says his wealth and earnings could not aid him in his hostility toward the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : في عداوته النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says they could not save him from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: الثاني : في دفع النار عنه يوم القيامة .
